articles.title: Madison Beer wins everyone over with her dance to celebrate a touchdown pass by Justin Herbert
articles.standfirst: Madison Beer steals the spotlight with her joyful reaction to Justin Herbert’s touchdown
articles.summary: Madison Beer steals the spotlight with her joyful reaction to Justin Herbert’s touchdown
articles.body:
Madison Beer gave Los Angeles Chargers fans something to smile about during an otherwise frustrating season opener, as cameras caught the singer enthusiastically celebrating fiancé Justin Herbert’s touchdown pass against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.

Beer was watching from a suite at SoFi Stadium as the Chargers opened their 2026 NFL campaign against Arizona.

When Herbert connected with wide receiver Ladd McConkey for an eight-yard touchdown in the third quarter, the pop star immediately jumped to her feet, raised her arms and danced with a huge smile.

The CBS broadcast captured the spontaneous celebration, and the moment quickly spread across social media. A clip shared online drew plenty of attention, with fans reacting to Beer’s energetic display as she cheered for Herbert .

Beer was dressed in Chargers colors and wore a customized No. 10 jersey representing Herbert’s number. Her appearance showed how closely she has followed the quarterback’s football career since their relationship became public.

The celebration came at a crucial point in the game. Herbert’s touchdown pass to McConkey cut Arizona’s advantage to just two points and briefly appeared to give Los Angeles the momentum it needed to complete a comeback.

Madison Beer’s celebration goes viral despite Chargers loss

Unfortunately for Beer and the Chargers, the excitement didn’t last. Arizona responded strongly in the fourth quarter and eventually secured a 26-14 victory, handing Los Angeles a surprising home defeat to begin the season.

Herbert finished the afternoon with 209 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception. His fourth-quarter pick proved particularly costly, helping the Cardinals close out an upset that few expected before kickoff.

McConkey was one of Herbert’s key targets, finishing with five receptions for 82 yards and the touchdown. The Chargers also got a rushing touchdown from rookie Omarion Hampton , but their offense couldn't produce another touchdown after Herbert’s scoring connection with McConkey .

On the other side, Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett threw for 277 yards and a touchdown, helping Arizona pull off one of the more unexpected results of the opening weekend.

While the Chargers' performance left fans disappointed, Beer’s celebration quickly became a separate talking point online. Social media users shared the clip of her jumping and dancing, with many joking about how happy she looked despite the eventual result.

Herbert and Beer made their relationship public in 2025, and the couple announced their engagement in July 2026. Beer has continued to support the quarterback, including by attending Chargers games and cheering him on from the stands.

Beer’s unfiltered excitement after Herbert found McConkey for the touchdown provided one of the afternoon’s most lighthearted scenes.

The Chargers will now look to regroup ahead of Week 2 after their unexpected loss. Herbert will be hoping for a stronger performance, while Beer’s enthusiastic presence could once again attract attention whenever the cameras turn toward the stands.

articles.title: Michael Irvin trolls Justin Herbert and fiancée Madison Beer after stunning loss
articles.standfirst: The Hall of Famer used Herbert’s relationship with Madison Beer to deliver a sharp postgame jab
articles.summary: The Hall of Famer used Herbert’s relationship with Madison Beer to deliver a sharp postgame jab
articles.body:
J ustin Herbert ’s relationship with Madison Beer became part of the conversation for all the wrong reasons after the Los Angeles Chargers suffered another ugly defeat.

Michael Irvin wasted little time piling on after the Chargers lost 26-14 to the Las Vegas Raiders at SoFi Stadium, using Herbert’s offseason travels with Beer to mock the quarterback’s inability to consistently move Los Angeles’ offense.

“You made the wrong drive,” Irvin said in a video posted to Instagram. “Driving your girl to the airport, but you can’t drive this team to that endzone?! That’s a problem.”

Irvin ’s social media team added another jab in the caption: “Mike thinks Justin Herbert is focused on the wrong drive.”

Los Angeles entered 2026 expecting a significant offensive improvement under new coordinator Mike McDaniel . Instead, the Chargers are 0-2 and Herbert has already found himself under growing scrutiny.

Herbert’s numbers reflect offensive struggles

Herbert finished the Raiders game 15-of-27 for 192 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He also fumbled three times as Las Vegas consistently disrupted the Chargers ’ rhythm and forced mistakes in key situations.

Through two games, Herbert has completed 59.3 percent of his passes for 401 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. His passer rating sits at 71.6, well below his career standards.

The Raiders added three sacks and nine quarterback hits, while rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses intercepted Herbert twice. Los Angeles did not help its quarterback, either. False starts, protection issues and additional fumbles repeatedly stalled drives.

Irvin ’s criticism may have been delivered as a joke, but the broader concern around Herbert and the offense is becoming increasingly serious.

Analysts starting to question Los Angeles

Irvin wasn't the only former player to take aim at the Chargers after the loss. Will Compton admitted he had badly misjudged what McDaniel would bring to Los Angeles.

“The Chargers have been brutal,” Compton wrote.

Herbert ’s struggles have made him an obvious target because of his status as the franchise quarterback and the expectations that come with it.

His relationship with Beer has attracted attention away from football as well, particularly after the couple spent time traveling overseas during the offseason.

None of that has anything to do with the turnovers or protection problems on the field, but Irvin clearly saw an opportunity to connect the two.

The Chargers need Herbert to rediscover the form that made him one of the league’s most highly regarded young quarterbacks.

Until that happens, a winless start means every mistake, and every joke, is likely to receive even more attention.

articles.title: Chargers fans blame Madison Beer and beer for QB Justin Herbert's rough start
articles.standfirst: Herbert endured another costly afternoon against Buffalo as Los Angeles remained winless
articles.summary: Herbert endured another costly afternoon against Buffalo as Los Angeles remained winless
articles.body:
Justin Herbert’s difficult start to the 2026 season has produced an increasingly familiar reaction whenever a star athlete’s performance dips: attention has shifted from what is happening on the field to who is waiting for him away from it.

The Los Angeles Chargers quarterback became engaged to singer Madison Beer during the summer, months before his team stumbled to an 0-3 start.

After Sunday’s 24-16 loss to Buffalo some fans began jokingly, and in some cases seriously, suggesting that Herbert’s relationship had become a distraction.

One fan compared Herbert unfavorably to former Chargers quarterback Ryan Leaf while referencing Beer , but the scrutiny has not been confined to social media. Hall of Famer Michael Irvin also questioned whether Herbert had enough focus on football.

“I come from an old school… where all focus must be on winning. Can’t have focus on anything else,” Irvin said. “You made the wrong drive. Driving your girl to the airport, but you can’t drive this team to that end zone?! That’s a problem.”

Herbert’s problems are showing up on the field

The football explanation is considerably less dramatic.

Herbert completed 20 of 34 passes for 226 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Buffalo, with the Chargers failing to capitalize despite their defense forcing five turnovers. Los Angeles reached the red zone four times but came away with only one touchdown and three field goals.

His interception was particularly costly. Herbert threw toward Marquez Valdes-Scantling near the goal line, only for C.J. Gardner-Johnson to step in front of the pass and return it 41 yards, helping Buffalo swing momentum late in the game.

Tom Brady was unsparing while analyzing the throw on the broadcast.

“Poor awareness, poor decision. Throws him a meatball sub,” Brady said.

Even Jim Harbaugh , who has consistently defended Herbert since becoming Chargers coach, delivered an unusually direct assessment the following day.

“Be better. Be better,” Harbaugh said of Herbert’s decision-making. “And that drives Justin, that drives me, that drives his position coach, that drives Mike [McDaniel], the coordinator. I mean, drives us all.”

Herbert has hardly been alone in the offensive struggles.

Dropped passes, stalled red-zone possessions and problems adjusting to coordinator Mike McDaniel’s new system have contributed to an offense averaging only 16 points through its first three games. Harbaugh nevertheless publicly backed McDaniel after the Buffalo defeat, insisting the organization still trusts its coordinator.

Herbert also accepted responsibility afterward rather than searching for excuses.

“Obviously not where we want to be,” he said. “It starts with me. I’ve got to play better and allow our offense to score more points.”

That leaves Beer as an easy target for frustrated fans, but there is nothing connecting the Chargers’ offensive failures to Herbert’s relationship.

Los Angeles has legitimate problems to solve at 0-3. Herbert’s decision-making is clearly among them, but blaming his fiancée offers a much simpler explanation than the football actually does.

articles.title: The five NFL teams on the verge of an 0-4 start, and why the daunting historical stat staring them in the face
articles.standfirst: The Los Angeles Chargers are the most surprising 0-3 team so far in the 2026 NFL season.
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are the most surprising 0-3 team so far in the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Back when there were only 16 games in an NFL season, an 0-2 start was considered a death sentence . Nowadays, with three Wild Card teams making the playoffs and 17 games on the schedule, things are a bit different.

An 0-2 start isn't the end of the world. An 0-3 start is now the new 0-2 start , but it also doesn't mean a team can't turn around their season. Going 0-4 and making the postseason would be almost unprecedented , though. The 1992 San Diego Chargers are the only team to have pulled off that feat, although they ended up getting destroyed 31-0 by the Miami Dolphins in the Divisional Round.

Los Angeles Chargers are the most surprising 0-3 team, followed by the Houston Texans

Heading into Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season, the Los Angeles Chargers are one of five teams staring an 0-4 record in the face. Three other AFC squads are in the same boat: Miami Dolphins , Tennessee Titans , and Houston Texans . Over in the NFC, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are the lone team in the conference still winless.

The Bucs are in dire straits at the moment. They just lost starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for multiple games, so their season might already be done and dusted. Meanwhile, no one expected the Titans or Dolphins to do much of anything this season , so an 0-4 start for either of them wouldn't be a surprise.

The Chargers and Texans are in another camp, though. Both came in with relatively high expectations, but both have shown major flaws. Chargers QB Justin Herbert has been hit with a lot of criticism this season, while the Texans defense was expected to be a historically great unit, which hasn't been the case.

In Week 4, these will be the teams standing in the way of the winless franchises: Dallas Cowboys (at Texans), Baltimore Ravens (vs. Titans), Green Bay Packers (at Buccaneers), Minnesota Vikings (vs. Dolphins), and Seattle Seahawks (vs. Chargers).

articles.title: Who is Kris Rhim? The ESPN reporter who drives Jim Harbaugh up the wall isn't backing down: "People want to know what's going on"
articles.standfirst: After a tense exchange with Jim Harbaugh, Kris Rhim explains why tough questions are part of his job
articles.summary: After a tense exchange with Jim Harbaugh, Kris Rhim explains why tough questions are part of his job
articles.body:
Kris Rhim has become a familiar face around the Los Angeles Chargers , and his latest exchange with Jim Harbaugh has put the ESPN reporter at the center of attention.

Rhim is ESPN's NFL Nation Chargers beat reporter, a role he's held since 2023. Before joining ESPN, he covered the Baltimore Ravens for The Baltimore Banner and previously worked with The New York Times fellowship program.

His job now involves following the Chargers closely, asking questions and explaining what happens around a team that entered 2026 with high expectations.

That responsibility has become particularly important during Los Angeles' miserable start.

The Chargers dropped to 0-4 after Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, with quarterback Justin Herbert struggling through another difficult afternoon.

Herbert threw two interceptions in the first half and was repeatedly pressured, although he responded with a much stronger second half. Harbaugh subsequently praised his quarterback's toughness and called the performance one of the grittiest he'd seen.

Rhim wasn't satisfied with that explanation and at Monday's press conference he challenged Harbaugh over the constant praise of Herbert's toughness, arguing that some of that toughness comes from the quarterback having to absorb too many hits.

"Jim, when you talk about ‘he’s a warrior’ and gritty, part of that is just [Herbert] taking a ruthless beating," Rhim said.

"I don’t know if it’s the group in front of him, his protection, what’s going on. But when you came here, your charge was to get him protected.

"But 2.5 years later, like you said, he still has to be a superhero for you guys to have a chance to win the game. Why is that?"

Why Kris Rhim isn't backing down

The Chargers coach said Rhim's comments sounded “more like an insult than a question” and returned to his belief in Herbert's resilience.

Rhim clarified that he wasn't insulting the quarterback and repeated that he wanted to know why Herbert remains among the league's most pressured passers. Harbaugh responded that he believed he'd already answered.

The exchange might've ended there, but Rhim later explained why he believes questions like that are part of his job.

He said he's never had significant issues with Harbaugh , players or other coaches and that covering a struggling team isn't necessarily worse. Instead, he believes difficult stretches create an even greater responsibility to find new angles and demand accountability.

“People want to know what's going on,” Rhim said.

That's the central point of Rhim's approach, as with the Chargers winless, Herbert under pressure and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel still backed by Harbaugh , there are legitimate questions surrounding the team's direction.

Harbaugh has publicly said McDaniel's job isn't in jeopardy, while Herbert's protection remains an obvious concern.

As for Rhim asking uncomfortable questions isn't about angering Harbaugh , but about explaining why a talented Chargers team has started 0-4.

articles.title: Is Madison Beer the reason behind Justin Herbert’s struggles? Chargers fans formulate wild theory
articles.standfirst: The Chargers are 0-5… and some fans are blaming Justin Herbert’s new relationship.
articles.summary: The Chargers are 0-5… and some fans are blaming Justin Herbert’s new relationship.
articles.body:
What seemed like a season in which they would improve significantly now appears to be the complete opposite. That is the story of the Los Angeles Chargers , even with the arrival of Jim Harbaugh and the presence of Justin Herbert , who is increasingly criticized for his poor performances.

Now the quarterback is once again the target of strong criticism, and a theory has resurfaced suggesting that his new relationship could be the real reason his level of play has dropped.

The Chargers have not won since Justin Herbert and Madison Beer’s picnic

There is a sector of fans who cannot forget a video from the Chargers’ training camp in which the two can be seen lying on the field, very close together, enjoying a genuine sunny day.

Now internet users and fans are bringing these images back up, saying that the team has not won since the video appeared, currently sitting at a negative 0-5 record , and worse still, with no signs that the season will improve.

A former champion criticized Herbert

Former Super Bowl champion TJ Ward pointed to Madison Beer’s presence in the stands as a possible factor behind Justin Herbert’s slow start to the 2026-27 NFL season.

Ward expanded on his comments during a recent episode of the Speakeasy podcast, where he criticized what he described as Beer’s “extra” reactions when the cameras focused on her during games.

"When you put your personal life in front of the world, it's up for critique. It's up for observation. And like I say all the time, I observe s___. And then I give it back to y'all.

"Has he gotten better or worse since they got together? When you talk about Justin Herbert most of the time this offseason, what is it surrounded around: football or his girlfriend?" Ward asked.

He then added, "Was she not at the game with revealing clothing on? And as soon as the camera got to her, she did a little extra."

articles.title: Chad Ochocinco's reaction to Madison Beer shows Justin Herbert might actually be too distracted: "Oh s**t, I get it"
articles.standfirst: There's a serious discussion ongoing on social media that the Los Angeles Chargers quarterback is having a bad season because of his celebrity girlfriend.
articles.summary: There's a serious discussion ongoing on social media that the Los Angeles Chargers quarterback is having a bad season because of his celebrity girlfriend.
articles.body:
One of the most stunning storylines in the NFL through Week 5 has been the Los Angeles Chargers being among the worst teams in the league. They were fully expected to be a playoff team, and quarterback Justin Herbert was considered a dark horse MVP candidate.

Instead, the team is currently 0-5 with a brutal schedule looming, and Herbert is in the midst of the worst season of his career . Naturally, fans want someone to point the finger at. New offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has been the scapegoat, yet second on the list is Herbert's girlfriend, Madison Beer .

There's a real ongoing conversation on social media that Herbert isn't fully focused on football because Beer is taking up too much of his spare time . Beer, of course, is a famous singer-songwriter and considered one of the most attractive women in the entertainment industry.

Chad Ochocinco is blown away after seeing picture of Madison Beer during live show

Despite her notoriety, former NFL player Chad Ochocinco actually didn't know what she looked like until his most recent podcast episode alongside Shannon Sharpe . Once Ochocinco looked up her pictures, he began to understand why Herbert might be struggling .

Sharpe isn't quite on the same page as Ochocinco. Sharpe says, " I don't get it ", seemingly opining that he doesn't believe Beer is attractive enough to truly steal away all of Herbert's attention. Regardless, Herbert and the Chargers need to find a way to turn their season around, and that will only happen if the main focus is on football by everyone involved.

Despite her notoriety, former NFL player Chad Ochocinco actually didn't know what she looked like until his most recent podcast episode alongside Shannon Sharpe . Once Ochocinco looked up her pictures, he began to understand why Herbert might be struggling .

Sharpe isn't quite on the same page as Ochocinco. Sharpe says, " I don't get it ", seemingly opining that he doesn't believe Beer is attractive enough to truly steal away all of Herbert's attention. Regardless, Herbert and the Chargers need to find a way to turn their season around, and that will only happen if the main focus is on football by everyone involved.

articles.title: NFL QB’s wife breaks the internet with stunning performance in Kim Kardashian’s new ad
articles.standfirst: Jake Browning’s wife turns heads with stunning new Kim Kardashian collaboration
articles.summary: Jake Browning’s wife turns heads with stunning new Kim Kardashian collaboration
articles.body:
Stephanie Browning is attracting plenty of attention online after showcasing her latest fashion collaboration with Kim Kardashian’s SKIMS brand, proving that her influence extends beyond the football sidelines.

The wife of NFL quarterback Jake Browning recently took to Instagram to share a series of photographs promoting NikeSKIMS, the fitness-focused collaboration between Kardashian’s shapewear company and sportswear giant Nike.

Stephanie opted for an all-black look featuring fitted leggings, a cropped jacket and a double-strap triangle sports bra. She completed the outfit with split-toe sneakers, posing for the camera while showing off the collection's athletic-inspired designs.

Her toned physique and cheerful expressions quickly caught followers' attention, with the post providing another glimpse into her growing fashion and lifestyle presence on social media.

“Gameday anywhere & everywhere in my NikeSKIMS,” she captioned the Instagram post.

The collaboration represents another opportunity for Stephanie to establish herself as an influencer in her own right.

She's previously attracted considerable attention for her distinctive game-day outfits while supporting Jake throughout his professional football career.

Stephanie Browning embraces new opportunities following Chargers move

Her latest fashion appearance comes shortly after the couple experienced another unexpected development in their NFL journey.

Jake recently joined the Los Angeles Chargers after initially signing with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the offseason. However, his time in Tampa Bay ended without a regular-season appearance before Los Angeles brought him into the organization.

The quarterback previously spent three seasons with the Cincinnati Bengals, primarily working as a backup to star quarterback Joe Burrow. His latest move has now opened an entirely new chapter for the couple.

Stephanie celebrated the news in a TikTok video, sharing her excitement about relocating to Los Angeles while reflecting on how unpredictable their lives have become.

“Oh, my god, I feel like my life is literally a series of, 'You cannot make this s*** up,'” she said as news coverage of Jake's Chargers signing appeared in the video.

However, Stephanie also offered an unusually candid perspective on her husband's uncertain NFL future.

“Jake could get cut tomorrow,” she admitted, explaining that the past few months had helped her discover more about herself and what she wanted to achieve professionally.

She added that moving to Los Angeles would allow her to concentrate on her own ambitions, particularly because the city has always been her favourite place to live.

The relocation is an opportunity for Stephanie to explore new professional possibilities and develop her influencer business independently.

Her latest NikeSKIMS collaboration demonstrates that she's already making the most of those opportunities, securing attention through fashion, fitness and lifestyle content.

Although Jake's position in professional football remains uncertain, Stephanie appears determined to build something of her own.

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh takes on the NFL and the Broncos for preventing Daiyan Henley from joining the Chargers
articles.standfirst: The Chargers coach is furious after Denver pulled out of an agreed trade for the linebacker
articles.summary: The Chargers coach is furious after Denver pulled out of an agreed trade for the linebacker
articles.body:
J im Harbaugh has made it clear that he believes the Denver Broncos should be held accountable after their proposed trade for Daiyan Henley collapsed, leaving the linebacker with the Los Angeles Chargers despite an agreement between the AFC West rivals.

The deal was reached shortly before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, November 10. Denver had agreed to send Los Angeles a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection in exchange for Henley, but the transaction was conditional on the linebacker passing his physical.

The Broncos announced late Wednesday that the agreement would not be completed. While the team initially offered no explanation, reports subsequently indicated that concerns emerged during Henley's medical examination, particularly involving his knee.

Harbaugh , however, believes the situation went beyond a routine failed physical. Speaking to reporters Thursday, the Chargers coach accused Denver of using the medical process as leverage to negotiate a cheaper deal after the deadline had already passed.

“The Broncos based a pass-fail on a medical grade, based on whether we would take less compensation, and we wouldn’t, and we didn’t,” Harbaugh told reporters.

“In my opinion, it’s one of those loopholes that the league should really look into because it sets a bad precedent, continues to set a bad precedent.”

The coach was particularly unhappy with the suggestion that the Broncos would have accepted Henley if Los Angeles had agreed to different draft compensation.

“It shouldn’t be [a loophole], but apparently it is,” Harbaugh said when asked about the Broncos allegedly trying to renegotiate terms after the deadline had passed.

“That’s why it’s a loophole and teams should not have the ability to do that. I mean, it’s a medical grade. It’s a pass-fail for a medical grade. They told us they weren’t going to pass him if it was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon, and they would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a fill in the blank. I don’t know what to call that. That’s what it is.”

Why the failed trade has become an NFL rules debate

The disagreement is about more than Denver losing a potential defensive addition. Under NFL rules, teams can revisit draft-pick compensation after the trade deadline when a physical raises medical concerns, although they cannot simply substitute another player into the transaction.

The Chargers believe that flexibility creates an opportunity for teams to pressure opponents into accepting less favorable terms after the deadline.

Denver's position is that the medical examination revealed information that had not been adequately reflected in the information provided before the agreement. An Associated Press report said the Broncos were surprised by findings during the physical and sought to discuss revised compensation after consulting medical personnel.

Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz disputed that account, saying Denver already knew Henley was dealing with an injury.

Henley had been an important contributor in Los Angeles. The 2023 third-round selection had started all eight games this season, recording 51 tackles, an interception, a forced fumble and two fumble recoveries.

He had also established himself as a productive starter over his first three seasons, making the proposed move to a division rival a significant decision for both teams.

For Henley , the failed agreement meant an unexpected return to the organization he had been preparing to leave. Harbaugh acknowledged the emotional impact of the uncertainty and insisted the Chargers had welcomed him back.

“What that put Daiyan through, you know, kind of the ringer for the last couple days. Yeah, it’s emotional. It’s painful,” Harbaugh said. “And all that’s considered, and should be considered by the league when they look into this loophole.”

The situation also recalls the Baltimore Ravens ' decision to cancel their proposed trade for Maxx Crosby earlier in 2026 after medical concerns emerged during his physical.

Harbaugh and Hortiz now want the league to examine whether its rules need changing. The Chargers have retained Henley for the remainder of the season, while Denver must look elsewhere for defensive reinforcements.

What began as a straightforward deadline transaction has become a dispute over how much freedom NFL teams should have to revisit deals once the clock has expired.
